transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Ng (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (Redwood Product Sec), Priya Shah (StraitPoint Head Eng), Evan Moore (StraitPoint SecOps), Rashid Khan (StraitPoint Cloud Arch), Nadia Flores (Compliance)

Summary (auto): Brief review of encryption controls for Redwood platform. Focus on BYOK/HSM, key lifecycle, audit log export, and POC requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we have about an hour. I'm lena from Redwood, i'm the account lead. Marcus and Janelle from our security and product teams are on to cover encryption and key mgmt.
[00:09] Priya Shah: Hi everyone, Priya here. We wanted to make sure we covered how keys are handled, whether we can bring our own keys, and basically the auditability piece for our internal regulators.
[00:18] Marcus Ng: Hi Priya, Evan, Rashid — quick agenda: cover at-rest and in-transit encryption, KMS options (hosted vs customer-managed), BYOK flow, HSM support, key rotation, and audit logs / SIEM export. then Q&A.
[00:33] Evan Moore: Great. quick callout up front — we need FIPS certified HSMs and also strong isolation for model weights, we can't have keys stored in a shared tenant outside our control.
[00:44] Janelle Park: understood. Redwood supports envelope encryption for model artifacts and customer data. keys can be customer-managed via our KMS integration. for HSM-backed keys we support standard KMIP and cloud provider HSM APIs depending on deployment.
[00:59] Rashid Khan: can you clarify: for hosted Redwood, is the key material ever in Redwood's control, or do you do a pure BYOK where the root never leaves our KMS/HSM?
[01:10] Marcus Ng: good q. For hosted we offer two patterns: 1) customer-managed keys in their cloud KMS — in that case, Redwood requests ephemeral data keys via API calls and never persists your master key; we only store encrypted data keys (envelope). 2) For strict control we support BYOK where the customer provisions a key on their HSM and we fetch wrapped DEKs. the root key stays in your HSM. There's also an on-prem/private deployment option where you run the control plane in your VPC and keys never transit our control plane.
[01:36] Priya Shah: ok so when you say 'fetch wrapped DEKs' — is the unwrap operation ever done on Redwood infrastructure? that is, do you send ciphertext to Redwood then Redwood unwraps?
[01:47] Marcus Ng: unwrap can be done two ways. if you give Redwood permission to call your cloud KMS, we can request plaintext DEKs briefly in-memory on our runtime nodes then securely erase. alternatively, for higher-assurance customers we do HSM remote signing/unwrapping via a gateway so the unwrapping happens in your HSM and only wrapped keys are sent to the runtime. the standard pattern is envelope encryption — we store only DEKs encrypted with your CMK.
[02:12] Evan Moore: and how about attestation or proof that keys were never exported? we need audit trails and ideally key ceremony logs.
[02:20] Janelle Park: we produce audit logs for all KMS API calls proxied through Redwood — timestamps, caller identity, operation type. for HSMs you should have your HSM logs and also we can provide integration guidance to forward logs, or we can pipe relevant Redwood-side events to your SIEM. but yeah, the proof-of-non-exfil is typically via HSM attestation, cloud provider audit logs, and our request logs.
[02:40] Nadia Flores: are you FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 compliant for your HSM integrations? our auditors expect FIPS validated crypto modules.
[02:47] Marcus Ng: Redwood itself doesn't ship an HSM product; we integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs — for example AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and vendor HSMs that are FIPS validated. If you run private deployment with a validated HSM in your environment, that satisfies the requirement. we'll provide the list of supported HSM vendors in the doc pack.
[03:05] Priya Shah: encryption in transit — are you using TLS1.3 only? we need mTLS for service-to-service inside the platform to enforce mutual auth.
[03:13] Janelle Park: we use TLS1.3 for all network encryption. for customer-to-Redwood connections we support mTLS and client cert based auth, plus optional PrivateLink/VPC endpoints for zero public egress. service-to-service inside Redwood uses mTLS/MTLS-like mutual auth plus short-lived certs from our internal CA.
[03:32] Rashid Khan: what about key rotation? we need quarterly rotation and ability to do emergency rotation with re-encrypt of persisted data and model weights.
[03:40] Marcus Ng: key rotation is supported at two layers — DEK rotation (automated periodic re-wrapping of data keys) and CMK rotation (you can rotate your CMK in KMS, we will re-wrap DEKs accordingly). for stored model weights, we have a background re-encryption job — note that re-encrypting terabytes of model cache can be time-consuming, we provide a streaming rewrap approach to allow incremental rotation to avoid big downtime.
[04:03] Evan Moore: streaming rewrap sounds good, what's the downtime assumption?
[04:07] Marcus Ng: usually zero downtime for read ops; writes during rotation continue. worst case small perf hit — depends on size, we'll help with a plan in the POC.
[04:17] Priya Shah: audit logs — retention and how we get them. we need 7 years for some regs, and logs need to be tamper-evident.
[04:25] Janelle Park: Redwood retains control-plane logs per customer config; default is 90 days but we offer extended retention add-ons. for tamper-evidence we sign logs with an append-only scheme and can deliver to your S3 or to a Syslog/Splunk/Elastic endpoint. we support streaming export to your SIEM via secure connector.
[04:44] Evan Moore: do you support immutable storage or write-once policies for logs?
[04:48] Marcus Ng: if you push logs to your S3, you can enable object lock / legal hold; we also support pushing to third-party archival systems. Redwood's internal logs are retention-configurable but for compliance, customers usually route to their own long-term store.
[04:59] Nadia Flores: SOC2 and ISO artifacts — can you share your Type II and certifications?
[05:03] Lena Ortiz: yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary. note some artifacts are redacted, but we can provide the report and certs, plus a gap questionnaire if needed.
[05:14] Rashid Khan: what about multi-tenant risk — are model weights, caches, or KV caches ever shared across tenants?
[05:20] Marcus Ng: we use strong tenancy isolation. model weights are either dedicated or per-tenant cache partitions depending on deployment. KV caches are namespaced. for Dedicated and Private customers you can get isolated pools. for hosted tenants we maintain strict memory isolation and OS/container hardening — we can share the architecture diagram.
[05:38] Priya Shah: region / data residency — our data must stay in EU for certain workloads. do you support region pinning?
[05:44] Janelle Park: yes, region pinning is supported. we can pin workload to EU regions and also provide private deployments in your cloud tenant to meet residency requirements.
[05:53] Evan Moore: one more — who has access to keys and logs inside Redwood org? we need RBAC and least privilege guaranteed.
[05:59] Marcus Ng: internal access is strictly RBAC'ed; admin console access requires SSO (SAML/Okta). access to key call data is limited to specific service accounts. we have audit trails for every human access event and we can provide a list of roles that have elevated rights.
[06:16] Priya Shah: what's the support for split knowledge or dual-control during key ceremonies? our policy requires two-person approval for key import/export.
[06:24] Janelle Park: for BYOK with HSM, you control the key import into your HSM and can enforce dual-control in your on-prem HSM. if you want Redwood to orchestrate imports we can support workflows that require two approvers via our admin ops process, but most customers keep that step fully in their control HSM.
[06:42] Nadia Flores: incident response — if a key is suspected compromised, what's the process?
[06:47] Marcus Ng: immediate steps: rotate impacted keys (we support emergency CMK rotation), revoke session tokens, and switch traffic to fallback keys/models. Redwood also supports canary rollback to a previous model variant. we'll provide runbooks and coordinate with your SecOps. we keep forensic logs and can support export for your investigation.
[07:04] Rashid Khan: any perf hit from encrypting/decrypting tokens or model requests? we need to understand CPU/GPU overhead for DEK operations and impact on latency.
[07:12] Marcus Ng: the cryptographic operations (KMS calls) are off the critical path in envelope pattern. runtime does an in-memory DEK decrypt which is very fast; most heavy work remains model compute on GPU. we measured 1-5% latency overhead for common setups. exact numbers depend on DEK caching and prefix/KV cache hit rates. we'll include benchmark numbers and run POC to quantify for your workload.
[07:36] Priya Shah: let's talk about the POC: we want to measure encryption overhead, key rotation scenario, and log export. what's needed from our side?
[07:44] Lena Ortiz: good. we'll need sample request patterns, a small dataset (PII redacted or synthetic), and an intended region. Marcus can provision a POC tenant with BYOK turned on and HSM-backed keys if you provide KMS credentials and acceptance to let Redwood call the KMS (or we can use remote unwrap gateway).
[07:59] Evan Moore: we prefer no plaintext leaving our KMS — so remote unwrap in HSM is preferred. we have Azure Dedicated HSM; can you integrate?
[08:07] Marcus Ng: yes we support Azure Dedicated HSM. we'll share the integration doc. remote unwrap via gateway requires a small connector in your VPC or an approved secure endpoint.
[08:17] Rashid Khan: network egress policy — we need assurance that logs and metric data do not leak PII. how do you scrub sensitive tokens?
[08:24] Janelle Park: Redwood has PII redaction at ingestion and can filter sensitive fields. for audit logs we don't emit full payloads; we capture metadata and allow configurable masking. in the POC we can teach the sanitizer rules.
[08:38] Priya Shah: one tangential item — model snapshots. when you persist KV cache or model snapshots to S3, are they encrypted with the same CMK?
[08:45] Marcus Ng: yes snapshots and persisted cache are encrypted via envelope encryption using your CMK. we can optionally use different keys per environment.
[08:52] Evan Moore: what about HSM-backed signing of artifacts for tamper evidence?
[08:56] Janelle Park: we support signing using HSM keys — you can require artifacts to be signed by your CMK on import/export and we store signature metadata.
[09:06] Priya Shah: are there any known caveats where secrets might land in logs?
[09:10] Marcus Ng: we try to avoid logging secrets; sometimes truncated identifiers appear. we'll provide the logging policy and redactors. if you find anything in POC we'll fix.
[09:18] Nadia Flores: auditors will ask for SLA on key usage logs — can you commit to specific retention in contract?
[09:23] Lena Ortiz: yes, retention is negotiable as part of the enterprise contract. we can include specific log retention and delivery terms.
[09:31] Evan Moore: one more question — do you support customer HSMs that are offline / air-gapped?
[09:36] Marcus Ng: air-gapped HSMs are supported in Private/on-prem deployments where you host the HSM and run our runtime locally. for hosted we need network connectivity to your KMS/HSM endpoint.
[09:48] Priya Shah: ok great. anything else on the security side?
[09:50] Janelle Park: probably worth noting our compliance program: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 alignment, periodic pen tests. we also support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning for RBAC.
[10:01] Rashid Khan: can we get a mapping doc of controls to SOC2/ISO clauses for our auditor?
[10:06] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll provide a controls mapping and the security questionnaire responses.
[10:11] Evan Moore: good. let's recap next steps.
[10:14] Lena Ortiz: recap: Marcus to share HSM integration and BYOK checklist; I will share SOC2/ISO pack and questionnaire. Priya/Evan to confirm POC dataset and region. schedule SecOps follow-up for key rotation and logs. we'll aim to have documents by EOD Friday.
[10:31] Priya Shah: sounds good, thank you.
[10:33] Rashid Khan: thanks everyone.
[10:34] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and drop the doc links.

(End of recording)
